working_title: Gravity Does the Work — Head, Pressure & Flow

owner_input.idea: Opportunity Intelligence spin-off: teach the transferable physics/function behind moving water without product-first thinking, so learners can determine whether gravity can do the job before buying pumps.
owner_input.owner_notes: Preserve Water Through the Layers at Product Design. Do not reopen the approved Water research foundation unless Product Design routes a specific evidence gap back.
owner_input.requested_angle: Function-first, evidence-first water movement: elevation/head, pressure, flow, friction, gravity, siphon, pump, testing and transferable system thinking.

websites_reviewed: https://academy.rebelranchministries.org (crawler retrieval failed; current Program Hub GitHub source reviewed as durable source of truth)
context_review.learning_area_reason: Head, pressure and flow are practical water/resource-system skills supporting irrigation, livestock, rainwater, household/homestead movement and resilient low-energy design.

conflicts_found: Ideal Bernoulli relationships do not account for real-system friction and fitting losses; field/design losses must remain visible.
Hazen-Williams is a useful water-system design relationship but is not a universal fluid-mechanics law.
Practical siphon lift is condition-dependent; an approximately 30-foot field limit must not be taught as an exact universal ceiling.
Historical gravity systems demonstrate transport/design capability but do not by themselves establish modern water quality or learner-specific suitability.
unresolved_questions: Product-stage exact learner calculator scope and assumptions
Product-stage hardware/device performance comparisons if recommended
